facts.label: Evidence against the leverage view and what would change it
facts.text: The strongest evidence against reading Elanco as slow to deleverage is operating momentum: reported revenue growth of 12.53% in the half-year, an issuer adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.9% against 21.2% a year earlier, and free cash flow of USD 206 million against USD 111 million. If that pace holds, EBITDA growth alone moves adjusted net leverage toward the issuer's year-end target of about 3.0x without debt repayment, although part of the revenue growth is AHV and currency rather than organic. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C13; calculation C27

facts.label: Evidence against the leverage view and what would change it
facts.text: The view improves if last-twelve-months cash interest shows cover above the FY2025 level, if the 2028 notes are refinanced or liquidity grows well beyond the 2028 maturities, or if the covenant calculation shows wide headroom. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Earnings depend on a handful of product lines and one channel partner rather than on any segment or country. Five products and product families supplied about 38% of FY2025 revenue, the Advantage Family alone about 10%, and the largest customer, an affiliate of Cencora, about 12%, with a second distributor at about 7%. The same customer owed USD 131 million at 2026-06-30, about 12.16% of receivables, so a change in that distributor's ordering or payment terms would move cash flow quickly. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern about concentration is momentum from new products: second-quarter organic constant-currency revenue growth of 8%, innovation revenue of USD 892 million in FY2025 against a raised 2026 target of USD 1,250 million, and Zenrelia described by the issuer as a blockbuster in the year to July. If these launches keep volume growth near the 7% of the half-year, the Seresto expiry is more likely to be absorbed than to be a cliff, which is an analyst interpretation. The view would change toward higher risk if volume growth fades before September 2027, if a generic Seresto entrant appears in the United States, or if the largest distributor shifts volume; it would change toward lower risk if the proxy statement and legal documents confirm independent directors, no holder above five percent and tight limits on distributions and priming. facts.label: Overall governance view
facts.text: Overall, Elanco presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the application of aqua sale proceeds to term loan debt and a refinancing that extended maturities, which matters because lower debt and a longer tenor reduce refinancing and liquidity risk and implies lower leakage risk for creditors. Countervailing evidence is the growth of other financing claims, namely the royalty sale liability, the headquarters lease option and the deferred and contingent AHV payments. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture. facts.text: - Refinancing the 2028 maturities is the central credit test. On the 2025 year-end schedule, scheduled principal is USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, then USD 1,236 million in 2028 and USD 548 million in 2029. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Revenue durability is the main business risk and the test has already started, which corrects the earlier Business & governance review. That review treated a United States generic Seresto entrant as a possible future event, but the 2025 annual report states that a competitor began selling a generic product competitive with the Seresto collar in January 2026, more than a year before certain patent rights expire, and that Seresto has had no patent protection in certain markets since 2025. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is momentum and the pace of deleveraging. Half-year adjusted EBITDA rose 21.01%, the issuer reports share gains for Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and its year-end target of about 3.0x needs only about USD 91.50 million less issuer net debt at the guidance midpoint, against USD 173 million of free cash flow in the second half of 2025. Guidance has been raised twice since February: the 2026 adjusted EBITDA range was USD 955 million to USD 985 million in February, USD 975 million to USD 1,005 million in May and is now USD 1,010 million to USD 1,035 million, so the slower second-half growth it implies may simply be conservative. Cash taxes rose to USD 225 million in 2025 mainly because of tax payments on the aqua sale gain, so FY2025 free cash flow likely understated the run rate, although the size of the one-off part is not stated. facts.label: Business model and ownership
facts.text: Elanco sells animal health products in more than 90 countries through one reportable segment, with Pet Health at 48.78% of FY2025 revenue (parasiticides, dermatology, vaccines and pain) and Farm Animal at 50.10% (feed additives, antibiotics, vaccines and enzymes for cattle, poultry, swine and sheep). Sales go through veterinary distributors, retailers and directly to producers, and the sections read give no contract duration or renewal rates, so revenue visibility rests on prescribing habits, brands and seasonal demand rather than on contracted backlog. For creditors, balanced end markets and a regulated animal-health product set support cash flow, while first-half seasonality, with 51.62% of FY2025 revenue arriving in the first half, makes cash and working capital swing within the year and makes the first half the season that decides the full-year debt service picture. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C23

facts.label: Business model and ownership
facts.text: Elanco is a listed Indiana corporation separated from Eli Lilly in 2019, with no sponsor and no controlling holder identified; holders above five percent, board independence and related-person dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The credit facilities are secured by a significant part of the group's assets and the 2028 notes are senior unsecured, so the structure ranks the notes behind secured lenders to the extent of the collateral, and the annual report says a default under the credit facilities could stop payments on the notes through a cash sweep; guarantor scope and the priority among secured facilities are not established. Financial policy so far has favoured creditors: no dividends are anticipated, although the policy may change at any time, the facilities restrict dividends, debt and liens, and the aqua proceeds repaid term loans. The offsetting signals are the issuer's statement that leverage below 3x unlocks greater capital allocation flexibility, the growth in claims outside the debt figure and the annual report's reference to activist shareholders as a risk to strategy; the governance risk level from Business & governance is medium because the evidence is incomplete rather than adverse. facts.label: Revenue durability and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is recurring and seasonal, moderately cyclical and concentrated, with no disclosed contract backlog. Price added 2% and volume 5% to FY2025 revenue growth of 6% after a 2% drag from the aqua sale, and in the half-year to 2026-06-30 volume added 7% and price 2%, led by Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro and AdTab with part of the volume from new customers. Growth that depends on launches is only as durable as clinic adoption of each product, so the credit implication is that earnings rest on the pipeline continuing to replace franchises that are losing protection. Concentration adds fragility: five products and families supply about 38% of revenue, the largest customer, an affiliate of Cencora, about 12% and the second distributor about 7%, and the same largest customer owed USD 131 million, 12.16% of receivables, at 2026-06-30, so a change in one distributor's ordering or payment terms would move revenue and cash quickly. facts.label: Revenue durability and pricing power
facts.text: Pricing power is modest. Price added 2% in both periods, and the annual report warns that generic competition may force lower prices, discounts or rebates; sales rebates and discounts were a liability of USD 450 million at 2026-06-30 and the auditor treats United States rebate estimates as a critical audit matter, so a change in accruals would move revenue and cash. Farm Animal revenue is exposed to regulation and consumer sentiment: shared-class antibiotics were 9% and animal-only antibiotics 15% of FY2025 revenue, with 89% of the animal-only amount from ionophores, and the European Union has restricted preventative antibiotic use since 2022. Revenue is not structurally declining on the evidence, with reported half-year growth of 12.53% and second-quarter organic constant-currency growth of 8%, but the Seresto exposure described in the key findings is the clearest case of a franchise that is already facing substitution. facts.label: Margin resilience and cost flexibility
facts.text: Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure but not against a sharp loss of parasiticide revenue. Gross margin was 55.0% in FY2025 against 54.9% in FY2024, with price and productivity offset by inflation and higher manufacturing costs, and 57.79% in the half-year against 57.40%, helped by mix and price despite higher inventory costs; the issuer guides adjusted gross margin to 55.2% to 55.6% for 2026. In the half-year 35.41% of the extra revenue reached adjusted EBITDA, which is operating leverage on the way up. The reverse follows on the way down: gross profit is 57.79% of revenue, so each USD 100 million of lost revenue removes about USD 57.79 million of gross profit, while selling costs of USD 830 million grew 12.01%, nearly as fast as revenue, partly to support launches and higher pay. facts.label: Margin resilience and cost flexibility
facts.text: Cost flexibility is real but arrives after the cash cost. The 2025 restructuring plan carries about USD 116 million of cash severance before savings of about USD 25 million in 2026 and USD 60 million in 2027, and the Elanco Ascend programme targets USD 200 million to USD 250 million of adjusted EBITDA savings by 2030; all of these savings are management estimates. Input inflation is passing through inventory into cost of sales, and tariffs are a small and uncertain item: an April 2026 proclamation on imported patented pharmaceuticals carves out certain animal-health products and is not expected to apply to the issuer until at least September 2026. facts.label: Cash conversion and capital intensity
facts.text: Conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow is moderate and improving. Free cash flow was USD 394 million in FY2024 and USD 284 million in FY2025, which is 42.01% of reported and 31.52% of adjusted EBITDA for FY2025, and USD 379 million over the last twelve months, or 37.56% of adjusted EBITDA. FY2025 was held down by capital spending of USD 276 million, 5.85% of revenue against 3.31% in FY2024, for the Elwood antibody plant, and by cash taxes that rose to USD 225 million from USD 140 million, mainly on the aqua sale gain; the last-twelve-months capital spending ratio is 4.74% after half-year spending fell to USD 84 million from USD 122 million on timing. The half-year absorbed USD 239 million of working capital as receivables rose to USD 1,077 million from USD 873 million, which should unwind in the second half if collections follow the usual seasonal pattern. facts.label: Cash conversion and capital intensity
facts.text: Capital spending flexibility over the maturity wall is not established, because maintenance and growth spending are not split. The Elwood expansion and two early-stage projects suspended in 2025 suggest that part of the spending is discretionary. Against that, the headquarters lease adds payments of about USD 17 million a year and a USD 250 million purchase option in 2030, and restructuring cash (the reserve is USD 86 million) and USD 100 million of deferred AHV cash must be paid first. The credit implication is that free cash flow supports the scheduled principal of USD 63 million a year easily, 6.02x, but does not by itself build liquidity to meet the USD 1,784 million due across 2028 and 2029. facts.text: - Rivalry is intense and is the force most likely to change credit quality. Zoetis, Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health and Merck Animal Health compete on quality, price, effectiveness and new products, and a generic Seresto competitor has sold in the United States since January 2026. facts.label: Downside path
facts.text: Financial transmission follows from operating leverage. Gross profit is 57.79% of revenue and selling costs rose 12.01% in the half-year, so lost revenue falls through close to the gross margin, adjusted EBITDA falls below the run rate of USD 388 million to USD 413 million that guidance implies for the second half of 2026, and free cash flow, which must also pay the USD 86 million restructuring reserve and the USD 100 million of deferred AHV cash, falls below USD 379 million. The leverage consequence is that adjusted net leverage stalls near 3.36x instead of reaching the issuer's 3.0x target, and the interest roll adds USD 14.89 million a year for each percentage point on an analyst estimate of USD 1,489 million of unhedged floating-rate debt. facts.label: Downside path
facts.text: The liquidity and refinancing consequence is the point of vulnerability. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million stays flat at best while USD 1,236 million falls due in 2028, the 2028 notes become a current liability within twelve months from August 2027, and refinancing would be attempted in a weaker market with an interest rate that moves up with downgrades. The evidence does not support a default path: scheduled principal is USD 63 million a year until 2028 and last-twelve-months free cash flow covers it 6.02x, so the supported outcome is higher refinancing cost and slower deleveraging, with liquidity distress avoided through 2028 if the revolver of USD 750 million remains available. Management levers are discretionary capital spending, selling and research costs, the restructuring and Ascend savings, withholding acquisitions, additional securitization capacity of about USD 165 million and early refinancing; there is no dividend to cut. The observable triggers are first-half 2027 Seresto and Pet Health volume, year-on-year adjusted EBITDA growth, and whether the 2028 maturities are addressed by the third-quarter 2027 report. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Elanco presents an adequate business profile supported by balanced pet and livestock revenue, launch-led volume growth and creditor-aligned behaviour, but credit quality is constrained by adjusted net leverage of 3.36x, concentration in a few products and one distributor, and claims outside the debt figure. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to free cash flow of USD 379 million over the last twelve months and light scheduled principal to 2028, although interest cover is flat. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding parasiticide earnings through the 2027 generic season and on market access for USD 1,236 million due in 2028. The primary downside path is generic erosion of Seresto and Advantage Family earnings coinciding with that refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, rating reports, peer figures and the third-quarter 2026 report. Whether the business profile is better or worse than typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peers are supplied, and the financial profile trend is improving. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Elanco is deleveraging mainly through earnings growth, not debt repayment, but creditors carry net debt of USD 3,388 million, 4.38x reported and 3.36x adjusted EBITDA, above the 3.1x the issuer reports.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C02; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C17; calculation C18

The cushion for creditors is thinner than the headline because the issuer's figure leaves out a USD 255 million finance lease. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million, cash plus the undrawn revolver, only just covers the USD 1,236 million falling due in 2028. Last-twelve-months interest cover cannot be calculated because six-month cash interest is not printed, and covenant headroom is not established because the credit agreement is not supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C14; calculation C29; calculation C12

### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Net leverage on carrying-value debt and reported EBITDA fell from 5.14x at the 2025 year-end to 4.38x at 2026-06-30, and on issuer-adjusted EBITDA from 3.85x to 3.36x. Pro forma for the AHV acquisition cash of USD 76 million paid on 2026-04-30, year-end net debt would have been USD 3,548 million and reported net leverage 5.25x; the June balance sheet already contains that payment, so the later figures need no adjustment.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C02; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C19

About four fifths of the 0.50x improvement in adjusted net leverage comes from higher EBITDA, with last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,009 million against USD 901 million for FY2025, and about one fifth from lower net debt of USD 3,388 million against USD 3,472 million. Holding EBITDA at the FY2025 level, net leverage would be 3.76x. Debt repayment is therefore not the engine: the issuer repaid USD 89 million of borrowings in the half-year while paying USD 76 million in cash for AHV.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C18; calculation C05

The gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is large and recurring. FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 676 million is USD 225 million below adjusted EBITDA, mainly special charges of USD 237 million, of which USD 156 million were restructuring charges, partly offset by USD 19 million of royalty revenue sold to a third party. Part of the restructuring is cash still to be paid, with the reserve at USD 86 million at 2026-06-30 against USD 124 million at 2025-12-31, so adjusted EBITDA overstates cash earnings until it is settled.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation C09; calculation C26
### Coverage and cash interest

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.28x in FY2025 against 4.68x in FY2024, but FY2024 reported EBITDA included a USD 640 million divestiture gain. On adjusted EBITDA cover rose to 4.37x from 3.07x, and the whole rise came from cash interest falling by USD 90 million to USD 206 million while adjusted EBITDA was flat at USD 901 million against USD 910 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C12

Cash interest of USD 206 million is net of USD 43 million received on net investment hedges; before that receipt it was USD 249 million and cover was 2.71x reported and 3.62x adjusted. Those hedge receipts depend on cross-currency swaps with tenors in 2026 and 2027, of which CHF 200 million was extended to 2031 in July 2026, so the benefit of the receipts will change as the swaps are rolled.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C20

The revolving facility requires pro forma adjusted EBITDA of at least 2.00 times cash interest expense and caps pro forma net debt at 7.71 times pro forma adjusted EBITDA. The issuer reports compliance with all debt covenants at 2026-06-30, but the covenant calculation is not printed and its definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not established.

Interest expense is rising for non-cash reasons and may rise in cash terms. Net interest expense was USD 116 million in the half-year against USD 88 million, with USD 29 million imputed on the sale of future revenue and the headquarters lease adding more. USD 2,300 million of pay-fixed swaps are scheduled to mature in August 2026 and USD 1,450 million of forward-starting swaps are scheduled to start then, so on Analyst Judgement about USD 1,489 million of floating-rate debt becomes unhedged and each percentage point of rates adds roughly USD 14.89 million a year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C21
### Cash-flow quality

Free cash flow was USD 284 million in FY2025 after capital spending of USD 276 million, which was lifted by the Elwood monoclonal antibody plant expansion, and USD 394 million in FY2024. Conversion of reported EBITDA into free cash flow was 42.01% in FY2025 against 28.45% in FY2024, and last-twelve-months free cash flow to 2026-06-30 is USD 379 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C13; calculation C27

In the half-year free cash flow was USD 206 million against USD 111 million, helped by capital spending of USD 84 million against USD 122 million, which the issuer attributes to timing. Working capital absorbed USD 239 million as receivables rose to USD 1,077 million from USD 873 million at year-end, and the single customer that is about 12% of revenue owed USD 131 million at 2026-06-30, so collections matter for the second half.

The 2025 annual report disclosed the AHV agreement signed on 2026-02-19, with USD 170 million of guaranteed payments, USD 70 million of them at closing, and up to USD 140 million contingent. At closing on 2026-04-30 the half-year report shows cash of USD 76 million, deferred cash of USD 100 million and contingent consideration valued at USD 67 million, a total purchase consideration of USD 243 million. ### Data-quality and definition risks

The main definition risk is the debt perimeter. The issuer's net debt of USD 3,159 million leaves out the USD 255 million headquarters finance lease that the balance sheet carries inside debt and starts from debt before USD 26 million of issuance costs, so counting the lease puts net debt USD 229 million higher and adjusted net leverage at 3.36x against 3.13x on the issuer's own inputs, which it prints as 3.1x.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C17

The source inventory in Source readiness agrees with these figures and lists no executed credit agreement, indenture, rating report or third-quarter 2026 report. Period risks follow. FY2024 reported EBITDA of USD 1,385 million includes the USD 640 million gain on the aqua sale, so FY2024 reported leverage is not a clean base; the half-year to 2026-06-30 includes AHV for two months; and last-twelve-months EBITDA is built from reported components with a USD 1 million rounding gap to the issuer's own adjusted figure. Interest paid, taxes paid and the maturity ladder are printed for years and not for the half-years.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation C05; calculation C07
### Evidence against the leverage view and what would change it

The strongest evidence against reading Elanco as slow to deleverage is operating momentum: reported revenue growth of 12.53% in the half-year, an issuer adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.9% against 21.2% a year earlier, and free cash flow of USD 206 million against USD 111 million. If that pace holds, EBITDA growth alone moves adjusted net leverage toward the issuer's year-end target of about 3.0x without debt repayment, although part of the revenue growth is AHV and currency rather than organic.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C13; calculation C27

The view improves if last-twelve-months cash interest shows cover above the FY2025 level, if the 2028 notes are refinanced or liquidity grows well beyond the 2028 maturities, or if the covenant calculation shows wide headroom. It worsens if restructuring cash and the deferred AHV payments pull free cash flow below the 2026 pace, if the scheduled August 2026 swap roll lifts interest cost materially, or if the third-quarter 2026 report shows adjusted EBITDA below the second-quarter run rate.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; Source readiness (CP-0)

Business and governance review of Elanco Animal Health Inc (Elanco) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway, covering business model, ownership, governance and behaviour, transactions and operating drivers from the filings supplied. Figures are in USD millions unless stated.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Elanco shows no documented shareholder extraction and no identified controlling holder, so creditor risk sits in business durability: five product lines supply about 38% of revenue, one distributor about 12%, and the Seresto collar loses its United States formulation patent in September 2027.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C09

Governance risk is rated medium because the evidence is incomplete, not adverse: the proxy statement, credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so board independence, ownership percentages and legal capacity for distributions or priming are not established. Behaviour so far is creditor-aligned, with divestiture proceeds applied to term debt, no dividends and a longer maturity profile, though other financing claims have grown: a USD 295 million royalty sale, a headquarters lease with a USD 250 million purchase option and deferred and contingent payments for the April 2026 AHV acquisition.
### Key findings

- Earnings depend on a handful of product lines and one channel partner rather than on any segment or country. Five products and product families supplied about 38% of FY2025 revenue, the Advantage Family alone about 10%, and the largest customer, an affiliate of Cencora, about 12%, with a second distributor at about 7%. The same customer owed USD 131 million at 2026-06-30, about 12.16% of receivables, so a change in that distributor's ordering or payment terms would move cash flow quickly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C09

- Revenue durability is weakest where patent cover is ending. The Seresto formulation patent expires in the United States in September 2027, its European formulation patents expired in June 2025, with supplementary protection certificates in some countries running to August 2026, and certain Advantage Family products, Rumensin and Maxiban and Monteban have no patent protection. Volume growth of 7% in the half-year to 2026-06-30 came from new products, led by Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, so creditors are relying on launches replacing eroding franchises.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C06

- Business risk is balanced between pets and livestock. Pet Health supplied 48.78% and Farm Animal 50.10% of FY2025 revenue, and the United States 47.38%, but pet health was 52.14% of revenue in the half-year and 51.62% of FY2025 revenue fell in the first half, so cash flow and working capital swing with the flea-and-tick season.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05

- Behaviour is creditor-aligned on the evidence available. The 2024 sale of the aqua business raised USD 1,294 million in cash, the vast majority used to repay term loan debt, the October 2025 refinancing extended the maturity profile, no dividends are anticipated and the credit facilities restrict them. The documented exceptions are other financing claims: the USD 295 million royalty sale, now a liability of USD 315 million, the headquarters finance lease and the deferred and contingent AHV payments.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C10

- No sponsor, fund vintage or sponsor fees apply because the issuer is a listed company, and no holder above five percent is identified in the filings supplied. Control, board independence and related-person dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so governance is described from the annual report only: eleven directors signed the annual report, the chair is not the chief executive, the auditor concluded that the statements present fairly and management assessed internal control over financial reporting as effective.

- Litigation is extensive but has not produced a recorded liability. A securities class action over Zenrelia safety, labelling and launch disclosures was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-03-26 and is on appeal, the related derivative suits are stayed, and the Tevra antitrust verdict for the issuer was affirmed on 2026-07-06; the issuer states it has established no material liability for these matters.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern about concentration is momentum from new products: second-quarter organic constant-currency revenue growth of 8%, innovation revenue of USD 892 million in FY2025 against a raised 2026 target of USD 1,250 million, and Zenrelia described by the issuer as a blockbuster in the year to July. If these launches keep volume growth near the 7% of the half-year, the Seresto expiry is more likely to be absorbed than to be a cliff, which is an analyst interpretation. The view would change toward higher risk if volume growth fades before September 2027, if a generic Seresto entrant appears in the United States, or if the largest distributor shifts volume; it would change toward lower risk if the proxy statement and legal documents confirm independent directors, no holder above five percent and tight limits on distributions and priming.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee membership, ownership percentages and related-person transactions are not established; this keeps the governance risk level at medium instead of low.

- The credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so the legal capacity for dividends, additional debt, liens and asset transfers is not established; the creditor-alignment conclusion rests on observed behaviour alone and cannot say what the issuer is permitted to do.
- Product revenue is given only for the top product families and product categories, so the concentration finding rests on the issuer's approximate shares and not on a full product schedule.

- Management characterisations of the innovation pipeline and the productivity programme are the issuer's own and are labelled as management language; they support the contrary view but do not change the evidenced risk.

### Overall governance view

Overall, Elanco presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the application of aqua sale proceeds to term loan debt and a refinancing that extended maturities, which matters because lower debt and a longer tenor reduce refinancing and liquidity risk and implies lower leakage risk for creditors. Countervailing evidence is the growth of other financing claims, namely the royalty sale liability, the headquarters lease option and the deferred and contingent AHV payments. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture.

Figures are in USD millions unless stated and the latest balance sheet is dated 2026-06-30.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Elanco is an adequate but stretched credit that is improving: adjusted net leverage has fallen to 3.36x mainly on higher earnings, yet liquidity of USD 1,280 million only just covers the USD 1,236 million due in 2028, so the 2027 refinancing is the test. A competitor has sold a generic Seresto collar in the United States since January 2026, so revenue durability, not near-term debt service, is the main business risk.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C18

The primary downside path is generic price pressure on parasiticides and a fade in launch volume while restructuring and acquisition cash arrive before savings, stalling deleveraging ahead of the 2028 maturities. Covenant headroom, legal priority and any rating are not established, and this review assigns no rating.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C06; calculation C21
### Key findings

- Leverage is falling because earnings are rising, not because debt is being repaid, and it is still high. Net debt of USD 3,388 million is 4.38x reported and 3.36x adjusted EBITDA, against the 3.1x the issuer reports, which leaves out the USD 255 million headquarters finance lease. Adjusted net leverage fell by 0.50x in the half-year, about four fifths of it from higher EBITDA, while the issuer repaid USD 89 million of borrowings and paid USD 76 million in cash for AHV.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C18

- Refinancing the 2028 maturities is the central credit test. On the 2025 year-end schedule, scheduled principal is USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, then USD 1,236 million in 2028 and USD 548 million in 2029. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million covers the 2028 amount 1.04x and the two years together only 0.72x, and the USD 750 million unsecured senior notes fall due on 2028-08-28, so the market window is 2027, the year Seresto loses its United States formulation patent. Management's target of at least USD 1,000 million of free cash flow over 2026 to 2028, on its own definition, would cover only 56.05% of the 2028 and 2029 maturities even if all of it were retained, so refinancing is needed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C26

- Revenue durability is the main business risk and the test has already started, which corrects the earlier Business & governance review. That review treated a United States generic Seresto entrant as a possible future event, but the 2025 annual report states that a competitor began selling a generic product competitive with the Seresto collar in January 2026, more than a year before certain patent rights expire, and that Seresto has had no patent protection in certain markets since 2025. Seresto and Advantage Family together supplied USD 593 million, or 21.65%, of half-year revenue and earn about 70% and 60% of their annual revenue in the first half, so the 2027 flea-and-tick season is the real test. The filings give no 2025 quarterly Seresto revenue, so erosion cannot yet be measured.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_elanco-20260331exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C22

- New-product volume is carrying earnings, and the guidance implies the pace will slow. Half-year volume grew 7% and price 2%, led by Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and adjusted EBITDA rose 21.01% with 35.41% of the extra revenue reaching adjusted EBITDA. Full-year guidance of USD 1,010 million to USD 1,035 million implies second-half adjusted EBITDA of USD 388 million to USD 413 million against USD 387 million a year earlier, growth of only 0.26% to 6.72%.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C16

- Debt service is covered, but cover is flat because interest is rising. FY2025 cash interest cover was 3.28x reported and 4.37x adjusted, and on income-statement interest the last-twelve-months cover is 4.07x adjusted against 4.10x for FY2025, so earnings growth is being absorbed by a 31.82% rise in half-year net interest expense. On an analyst estimate, about USD 1,489 million of floating-rate debt would be left unhedged after the swap roll scheduled for August 2026, adding USD 14.89 million a year for each percentage point, while free cash flow of USD 379 million over the last twelve months covers the USD 63 million of scheduled principal 6.02x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C05; calculation C12

- Claims outside the debt figure add obligations that the leverage ratios do not show. The liability for the royalty sale is USD 315 million at an 18.3% effective rate, AHV carries USD 100 million of deferred cash and contingent consideration of USD 67 million at fair value, the restructuring reserve is USD 86 million and the headquarters lease ends with a USD 250 million purchase option in 2030.

The strongest evidence against caution is momentum and the pace of deleveraging. ### Business model and ownership

Elanco sells animal health products in more than 90 countries through one reportable segment, with Pet Health at 48.78% of FY2025 revenue (parasiticides, dermatology, vaccines and pain) and Farm Animal at 50.10% (feed additives, antibiotics, vaccines and enzymes for cattle, poultry, swine and sheep). Sales go through veterinary distributors, retailers and directly to producers, and the sections read give no contract duration or renewal rates, so revenue visibility rests on prescribing habits, brands and seasonal demand rather than on contracted backlog. For creditors, balanced end markets and a regulated animal-health product set support cash flow, while first-half seasonality, with 51.62% of FY2025 revenue arriving in the first half, makes cash and working capital swing within the year and makes the first half the season that decides the full-year debt service picture.

Elanco is a listed Indiana corporation separated from Eli Lilly in 2019, with no sponsor and no controlling holder identified; holders above five percent, board independence and related-person dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The credit facilities are secured by a significant part of the group's assets and the 2028 notes are senior unsecured, so the structure ranks the notes behind secured lenders to the extent of the collateral, and the annual report says a default under the credit facilities could stop payments on the notes through a cash sweep; guarantor scope and the priority among secured facilities are not established. Financial policy so far has favoured creditors: no dividends are anticipated, although the policy may change at any time, the facilities restrict dividends, debt and liens, and the aqua proceeds repaid term loans. The offsetting signals are the issuer's statement that leverage below 3x unlocks greater capital allocation flexibility, the growth in claims outside the debt figure and the annual report's reference to activist shareholders as a risk to strategy; the governance risk level from Business & governance is medium because the evidence is incomplete rather than adverse.

### Revenue durability and pricing power

Revenue is recurring and seasonal, moderately cyclical and concentrated, with no disclosed contract backlog. Price added 2% and volume 5% to FY2025 revenue growth of 6% after a 2% drag from the aqua sale, and in the half-year to 2026-06-30 volume added 7% and price 2%, led by Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro and AdTab with part of the volume from new customers. Growth that depends on launches is only as durable as clinic adoption of each product, so the credit implication is that earnings rest on the pipeline continuing to replace franchises that are losing protection. Concentration adds fragility: five products and families supply about 38% of revenue, the largest customer, an affiliate of Cencora, about 12% and the second distributor about 7%, and the same largest customer owed USD 131 million, 12.16% of receivables, at 2026-06-30, so a change in one distributor's ordering or payment terms would move revenue and cash quickly.

### Margin resilience and cost flexibility

Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure but not against a sharp loss of parasiticide revenue. Gross margin was 55.0% in FY2025 against 54.9% in FY2024, with price and productivity offset by inflation and higher manufacturing costs, and 57.79% in the half-year against 57.40%, helped by mix and price despite higher inventory costs; the issuer guides adjusted gross margin to 55.2% to 55.6% for 2026. In the half-year 35.41% of the extra revenue reached adjusted EBITDA, which is operating leverage on the way up. The reverse follows on the way down: gross profit is 57.79% of revenue, so each USD 100 million of lost revenue removes about USD 57.79 million of gross profit, while selling costs of USD 830 million grew 12.01%, nearly as fast as revenue, partly to support launches and higher pay.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is average and improving, with leverage the weakest part. Scale is treated as average because last-twelve-months revenue of USD 5,020 million cannot be compared with peers, none being supplied. Competitive advantage is average, resting on approvals and patents for new franchises and weaker for off-patent products. Business diversification is balanced by end market and geography but concentrated by product and distributor. Cost and capex flexibility is limited in the short run by selling and research costs and partly discretionary capital spending, and margin stability is average, with gross margin of 57.79% in the half-year and clear operating leverage in both directions.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

- Short term, over 12 to 24 months, deleveraging should continue in 2026 and then meet the Seresto patent expiry and the 2028 refinancing. The issuer guides 2026 revenue to USD 5,090 million to USD 5,140 million and adjusted EBITDA to USD 1,010 million to USD 1,035 million, raised from USD 955 million to USD 985 million in February, with year-end net leverage of about 3.0x on its own definition against 3.1x to 3.3x in February; guidance implies slower second-half growth than the first half, restructuring savings add about USD 25 million in 2026 and USD 60 million in 2027, about USD 60 million of deferred AHV cash is due in January 2027, and the 2028 notes come within twelve months of maturity in August 2027. The credit implication is that 2027 carries three events at once: the patent expiry, the AHV payment and the refinancing window.

### Downside path

The downside is issuer-specific and runs through the 2027 flea-and-tick season. The initiating condition is broader generic competition against Seresto, whose United States formulation patent expires in September 2027 after a generic competitor began selling in January 2026, together with price pressure on the Advantage Family products that already lack patent protection. The first operational break is rebates and discounts needed to hold distributor and retailer shelf space and volume growth falling from 7% towards the 2% price effect, on a parasiticide base of USD 593 million of half-year revenue for these two brands, Seresto and the Advantage Family.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C06; calculation C08

Financial transmission follows from operating leverage. Gross profit is 57.79% of revenue and selling costs rose 12.01% in the half-year, so lost revenue falls through close to the gross margin, adjusted EBITDA falls below the run rate of USD 388 million to USD 413 million that guidance implies for the second half of 2026, and free cash flow, which must also pay the USD 86 million restructuring reserve and the USD 100 million of deferred AHV cash, falls below USD 379 million. The leverage consequence is that adjusted net leverage stalls near 3.36x instead of reaching the issuer's 3.0x target, and the interest roll adds USD 14.89 million a year for each percentage point on an analyst estimate of USD 1,489 million of unhedged floating-rate debt.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C09; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C05; calculation C15

The liquidity and refinancing consequence is the point of vulnerability. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million stays flat at best while USD 1,236 million falls due in 2028, the 2028 notes become a current liability within twelve months from August 2027, and refinancing would be attempted in a weaker market with an interest rate that moves up with downgrades. The evidence does not support a default path: scheduled principal is USD 63 million a year until 2028 and last-twelve-months free cash flow covers it 6.02x, so the supported outcome is higher refinancing cost and slower deleveraging, with liquidity distress avoided through 2028 if the revolver of USD 750 million remains available. Management levers are discretionary capital spending, selling and research costs, the restructuring and Ascend savings, withholding acquisitions, additional securitization capacity of about USD 165 million and early refinancing; there is no dividend to cut. The observable triggers are first-half 2027 Seresto and Pet Health volume, year-on-year adjusted EBITDA growth, and whether the 2028 maturities are addressed by the third-quarter 2027 report.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Elanco presents an adequate business profile supported by balanced pet and livestock revenue, launch-led volume growth and creditor-aligned behaviour, but credit quality is constrained by adjusted net leverage of 3.36x, concentration in a few products and one distributor, and claims outside the debt figure. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to free cash flow of USD 379 million over the last twelve months and light scheduled principal to 2028, although interest cover is flat. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding parasiticide earnings through the 2027 generic season and on market access for USD 1,236 million due in 2028. The primary downside path is generic erosion of Seresto and Advantage Family earnings coinciding with that refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, rating reports, peer figures and the third-quarter 2026 report. Whether the business profile is better or worse than typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peers are supplied, and the financial profile trend is improving.
